FRI-MON, 10/23-26: SKINT WEEKEND
🎃
halloween is still a week away, but the spooky season is already in full swing!
we’ve rounded up more than 40 halloween parties, shows, cover band concerts, screenings, pet parades, and more happening this weekend. check ’em out
here
.
cultural fests / food events / markets / shopping events
(free admission, unless noted otherwise):
► fri 10am-5pm:
sixth annual cider village at the union square greenmarket
: union square park, manhattan.
>>
► fri + sat (fri 1-7pm, sat 11am-6pm):
threadbare vintage clothing + antique textiles show
: 26 bridge street, brooklyn (dumbo). $15 admission.
>>
► sat + sun (11am-6pm):
fad (fashion art design) pop-up market
: st. paul’s church (boerum hill/cobble hill).
>>
► sat 11am-9pm:
the 11th annual diwali times square
: broadway from 46th st to 48th st.
>>
► sat 12-6pm:
the 12th diwali on hudson
: exchange place in jersey city.
>>
► sat 11am-4pm:
the third annual offset art book fair
: sheila c. johnson design center at parsons school of design (greenwich village). timed ticket required.
>>
► sun 11am-4pm:
maum market: asian makers market
: industry city (brooklyn).
>>
► sun 11am-6pm:
five boro foto fest: photographs, prints, zines, books, and mixed media
: culture lab lic.
>>
film fests / series
:
► fri + sat:
12th nordic international film festival
: scandinavia house (ues), $13 general, 50% off for students with code ‘student’
>>
► fri thru 10/29:
william greaves 100
:
once upon a time in harlem, symbiopsychotaxiplasm: take one, nationtime, lost boundaries
, and more. film forum (south village), $18.
>>
► fri thru 10/29:
area coded: american regionalism in film
:
giant, grey gardens, move ya body: the birth of house, shakedown, the texas chain saw massacre
, and more.
>>
sponsored
Photo: Roy Cox
Get $10 General Admission tickets and bring the kids FREE to hear one of the “greatest quartets of the last 100 years” (BBC) –
Dover Quartet
– on Halloween night at the historic Washington Irving campus near Union Square! Doors open at 6:45 and the concert begins at 7:30 PM.
Peoples’ Symphony’s former Resident Ensemble returns to the series’ longtime home with a soulful program of quartets by Dvořák and Brahms and a special orchestration of Rattle Songs (Pura FE) by indigenous composer Jerod Impichchaachaaha’ Tate.
Dover Quartet
is a two-time Grammy-nominated string quartet based in Philadelphia at the Curtis Institute of Music.
Founded in 1900,
Peoples’ Symphony Concerts
is New York City’s oldest chamber music series, offering affordable top-quality concerts for as little as $10 each. Learn more about our 127th Season at
PSCNY.ORG
.
SATURDAY, OCTOBER 31
Dover Quartet
Doors: 6:45 PM
Concert: 7:30 PM
40 Irving Place, between 16th & 17th Sts, Manhattan
GET TICKETS
friday
sponsored
: fri thru 10/25 (+ 10/30-11/1):
get $35 tickets to
the ripple, the wave that carried me home
at playwrights horizons!
: it’s 1960s kansas, and janice’s parents are fighting for the integration of public swimming pools — a fierce civil rights struggle that overshadows her childhood and drives a wedge between janice and her family. it’s also 30 years later, when janice is asked to speak at a ceremony honoring her father, forced to reckon with the scars of a past she has tried to forget. a piercing, theatrically vivid story about the personal toll of fighting for justice, and the ultimate challenge of forgiveness. get $35 tickets (incl. fees) with code ‘ripplesk’ for tier 1 and tier 2 tickets for friday-sunday performances through 11/1.
>>
sponsored
: fri thru 10/29: ditch the ordinary and discover some of nyc’s most unique experiences with
new york adventure club!
:
• watch medieval knights battle it out in a thrilling, full-contact armored combat experience
>>
• go behind the scenes of temple emanu-el, one of the world’s largest synagogues
>>
• unleash your inner artist at an after-hours pastel painting workshop inside the akc museum of the dog
>>
• and more!
>>
sponsored
: fri + sat (various times):
flop house comedy club
: nyc’s friendliest indie comedy club—with great comics and a cozy atmosphere—has some incredible lineups this weekend! save 50% with promo code ‘skint’ on tickets to these shows at 362 grand street in williamsburg: friday 8pm, 9:30pm, and 11pm; and the east village location is back at 201 allen st store 2 friday + saturday at 8:00pm. new: monthly member’s pass ($20) to see as many shows as you want + happy hour drinks + secret drop in announcements!
>>
fri 6-9pm:
housing works fifth annual taylor swift karaoke competition
: grab the mic and unleash your inner swiftie at the same housing works bookstore featured in the ‘all too well (taylor’s version)’ music video. singers can compete for gift cards, and all attendees will be entered in a raffle to win a $200 ‘stolen lullabies’ vinyl variant of
folklore
. housing works bookstore (soho), $10 adv, $15 door.
>>
fri 7pm:
looking for laughs
:
love island
meets
whose line is it anyway
? two blindfolded singles meet four comics for a real blind date. on stage. hosted by douglas widick and tess tregellas. caveat (les), $14.43 with promo code ‘skint15’ (reg. $22-23).
>>
fri 8:30pm:
bitches brew comedy show
: this women-produced-and-hosted comedy show conjures up big laughs in the back room of halyards (gowanus). tonight’s lineup includes matt koff (
the daily show
), hoodo hersi (
colbert
), julia shiplett (netflix), oba olaniyi, olivia stadler, and andrea allen. free admission (a tip jar will be passed around at the end of the show).
>>
fri 9:30pm:
yesterday’s horoscope, live!
: the stars are aligned for yesterday’s horoscope, a cosmic comedy show with an astrological bent, hosted by ‘the all seeing, all knowing, and occasionally withholding skies’ (kristina gustovich and jane mitchell). $15.67 with promo code ‘mamalovesskint’ (reg $24-25).
>>
saturday
sat + sun (11am-6pm):
lincoln center open house
: get a taste of lincoln center’s performing arts programming with a day of family-friendly performances, workshops, storytelling, music, dance, puppets, costume-making, and more, including jazz from jazz at lincoln center, an opera workshop with the metropolitan opera, and dance workshops from the school of american ballet and new york city ballet. free admission.
>>
sat 10am:
brooklyn’s black trailblazers: cemetery trolley tour
: visit the memorials of artist jean-michel basquiat, civil rights activists grace nail johnson and james weldon johnson, mathematician charles l. reason (the first black college professor in the united states), and other visionaries on this guided tour of green-wood cemetery examining the life and accomplishments of prominent black brooklynites. free admission (rsvp).
>>
sat 4pm:
we’re ready to (dis)believe you: (conspiracy) theories debunked
: stand-up comedy, true stories, live music, and bs-detector games meet neuroscience in a live variety show exploring why our brains fall for conspiracy theories and misinformation, and how you can build a sharper bs detector of your own. hosted by gabriel berezin of the
fugues
podcast. caveat (les), $14.64 with promo code ‘brokebuthappy’ (reg. $20.09).
>>
sat 5pm:
relationsh*t storytelling show
: stories about all kinds of relationships meet on-stage advice from actual therapists. hosted by lynn bixenspan and morgan pielli. q.e.d. (astoria), $12.
>>
sat 9:30pm (monthly):
drunk planet earth
:
mst3k
meets
animal planet
meets drinking game at this participatory show that revolves around watching an animal documentary, drinking, and the audience trying to stump the hosts with animal trivia. hosted by brian morabito and stephen buckley. caveat (les), free admission.
>>
sunday
sun 2pm (+ 2/7, 3/18, 5/2):
the broadway bach ensemble: fall concert
: the broadway bach ensemble, a community orchestra that presents four free concerts of music from the baroque era to the 21st century every year, kicks off its 42nd season with an afternoon program featuring works by grace williams, igor stravinsky, and robert schumann at the broadway presbyterian church (morningside heights).
>>
sun 7:30pm:
poetry overnight at bam
: bam’s first-ever poetry overnight takes over the adam space (bamcafé) for an all-night poetry reading, with featured readers, special guests, and unique collaborations until sunrise. come and go as you please, or stay for the whole event. curated by bam curator at large and macarthur ‘genius’ hanif abdurraqib and hosted by jon goode. brooklyn academy of music (fort greene), free admission.
>>
sun 8:30pm:
improv with my friends from work
: ceara jane o’sullivan (
snl, petty crimes podcast
) hosts a long-form improv show with cast and writers from
saturday night live
. ucb (east village), $20.
>>
monday
mon 6pm:
get lit! t kira madden and fenne lily
: author t kira madden joins wnyc’s
all of it
host alison stewart for a discussion about her debut novel,
whidbey
. the conversation will be followed by a musical performance from folk singer-songwriter fenne lily. nypl’s stavros niarchos foundation library (midtown), free admission.
>>
mon 7pm:
the story collider
podcast science storytelling show: ‘stepping up’ edition
: science meets storytelling. five storytellers take the stage with true tales about how science impacted their lives in touching, funny, and interesting ways. tonight’s edition explores stories about stepping up, from coming of age to fulfilling expectations. hosted by diana li and paula croxson. caveat (les), $14.22 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $24-25).
>>
mon 7:30pm (monthly thru may):
24th annual music mondays concert series
: the music mondays concert series returns with a new season of classical and contemporary chamber music at advent lutheran church (uws). tonight, claremont trio and clarinetist kinan azmeh perform works by azmeh, rebecca clarke, and maurice ravel. a casual reception will follow the performance. free admission (note: if online reservations are sold out, there will be a standby line).
>>

: hitchcocktober, the amazing maize maze, and more.

40+ PRE-HALLOWEEN WEEKEND EVENTS: 10/23-26
halloween is still a week away, but the spooky season is already in full swing!
we’ve rounded up more than 40 halloween parties, shows, cover band concerts, screenings, pet parades, and more happening this weekend (10/23-26).
the roundup is broken out into four sections:
• parties + events
• tribute bands
• movie-related
• pets
note: events marked with a pumpkin
🎃
will have a costume contest.
parties + events
10/23-24 (8pm):
the hidden jewel box presents:
haunted
: an immersive evening of burlesque, dance, and theater. the hidden jewel box theater (a tiny theater hidden inside port authority), $40 admission includes two refreshments.
>>
10/23 7pm:
tin can contingency and brainrot radio present: the third annual horror night
: a live reading of
the blob
recorded live for the airwaves, followed by performances from bands trash rabbit and nej. purgatory (bushwick), $12 adv, $15 door.
>>
10/23 7pm + 9:30pm:
the drunk texts presents: a halloween drunk double feature:
all hallow’s eve or, the tragedy of michael myers
+
thou wilt scream
: shakespearean adaptations of
halloween
(7pm) and
halloween
(9:30pm) with drinking games, improvisation, and audience participation. the rat nyc (dumbo), $12.
>>
10/23 10:30pm:
hand to phone – the halloween party
: ebm / house / dark dance with performances by the treasury, blood handsome, and heavy halo, plus an after-party with dj ivy oh. alphaville (bushwick), $15.
>>
10/24-25 (10am-5pm):
pumpkin point
: governors island’s annual pumpkin patch and fall festival. free admission.
>>
10/24 12-6pm:
lavender scare: a halloween-themed lesbian market + halloween party
: yume (flatbush), free admission.
>>
10/24 2-7pm:
beats for treats halloween block party
: saint james joy (father-son duo dj chill and dj jo vill) hits the decks with a special halloween block party. costumes optional. saint james place between gates ave + greene ave (clinton hill). free admission.
>>
10/24 3-6pm (market) + 6:30pm (movie):
scream scene presents a halloween market and
halloween
movie screening
: pine box rock shop (bushwick). free admission.
>>
10/24 7pm-2am:
halloween vinyl nights zombie skate night
: with ‘thriller’ dancers and djs misbehaviour, rizzskates, and cindy kim. xanadu (bushwick), $26.78 + $8 skate rental (or byo).
>>
10/24 8-10pm:
switch n’ play presents: slash n’ spray
: drag, burlesque, and queer performance. littlefield (gowanus), $20 adv, $25 day of.
>>
10/24 10pm:
final girl
: a drag show homage to your fave horror films. 9 bob note @ 3 dollar bill (east williamsburg), $25.
>>
10/24 11pm:
music for the masses: an ‘80s new wave halloween party
: tv eye (ridgewood), $20.
>>
🎃 10/24 11pm:
the black parade [halloween edition] emo + pop punk nite
: the brooklyn monarch (east williamsburg), $15.
>>
10/25 12-6pm:
saint vitus halloween market
: saint vitus (ridgewood), free admission.
>>
10/25 2:15pm:
talkdeath’s sixth annual halloween cemetery scavenger hunt
: green-wood cemetery, free admission.
>>
10/25 7pm:
raising hell: a halloween comedy fundraiser
: a standup fundraiser in partnership with callen-lorde, nyc’s lgbtq+ community health center since 1969. halloween costumes optional. brooklyn comedy collective (williamsburg), $15 (25% of ticket sales will benefit the center).
>>
10/25 9-11pm:
a very buffy halloween
: a dragstravaganza of your favorite characters from buffy the vampire slayer. bar freda (ridgewood), $15.24.
>>
10/26 7pm (+ 11/24):
green-wood cemetery moonlight tour
: green-wood (brooklyn), $30.
>>
10/26 8pm-mindnight:
scuff queer country dancing presents: goth nite featuring y’allternative rodeo
: the brooklyn monarch (east williamsburg), $20+.
>>
tribute bands
10/23 7pm-late:
the cure halloween party
: a cure music video dj set followed by tributes to bauhaus, siouxsie + the banshees, and the cure. bowery palace (east village), $15 (free dance party at 11pm).
>>
10/23 8:15pm doors:
ridgewood ghoul-o-rama ‘25
: tributes to the fall, the ‘early’ beatles, and the
singles
soundtrack. costumes encouraged. footlight underground at the windjammer (ridgewood), $15 suggested donation.
>>
🎃 10/24 6pm:
hllwn shw
: tributes to fleetwood mac, nirvana, my chemical romance, green day, the beatles, and the
scott pilgrim vs. the world
soundtrack, plus djs spinning emo, punk, and ska. bar freda (ridgewood), $13.18.
>>
🎃 10/24 7pm:
werewolf bar mitzvah iv: spookier, scarier
: tributes to bikini kill, yeah yeah yeahs, the cranberries, weezer, cibo matto, and rudimentary peni. hosted by dj tk. purgatory (bushwick), $15-18.
>>
movie-related
10/23-11/8:
terence fisher: hammer’s master smith
:
the brides of dracula, the curse of frankenstein, the gorgon, horror of dracula, the hound of the baskervilles
. metrograph (les), $18.
>>
10/23-11/4:
screen slate presents: psycho-fiction, the surreal nightmares of special effects artist screaming mad george
:
freaked, a nightmare on elm street 4: the dream master, bride of re-animator, big trouble in little china
, and more. roxy cinema (tribeca), $19.
>>
10/23-11/1:
troma-geddon
:
the toxic avenger, class of nuke ’em high, cannibal! the musical
, and more. anthology film archives (east village), $14 general, $10 seniors/students.
>>
10/23-11/1:
halloween events at film noir cinema (greenpoint)
: smootaphilia: erotic horror sinema, the 14th annual secrets of the dead short horror film festival,
nosferatu
with live music by olsen, a halloween party + secret horror screening,
the day after halloween
, and more. various prices.
>>
10/23-31:
halloween, suspiria, the texas chainsaw massacre
,
nosferatu
+ live score,
vampyr
+ live score
: roxy cinema (tribeca), $19-25.
>>
10/23 6pm:
paddle-in movies with gowanus dredgers
:
creature from the black lagoon
(1954). meets at the gowanus dredgers boathouse; the screening takes place on the gowanus canal. free-$25.
>>
🎃 10/23 7:30pm:
cemetery cinema presents:
horror of dracula
(1958)
: plus live music by in flesh and spirit. hosted by baron misuraca. bonus: free popcorn. coney island usa, $14.
>>
10/24-31:
magic, the exorcist, the wolf man, vampire’s kiss, nosferatu
(with live piano accompaniment)
: museum of the moving image (astoria). $17.50 general, $12 seniors/students.
>>
10/24-31:
zero vision cinema + astoria horror club’s halloweek
: a week of free spooky events in astoria + lic, including screenings, live music, scaryoke, comedy, a halloween party, and more.
>>
10/24 5pm:
bad movie night brooklyn presents:
ernest scared stupid
(1991)
: food and drinks will be available for purchase. freddy’s bar (south slope), free admission.
>>
10/24 8pm (7pm pre-show):
the rocky horror picture show
shadowcast + tim curry tribute
: brooklynone productions (industry city). free admission (donations welcome), $15 after-party.
>>
10/25 2:30pm:
the silent clowns film series presents:
the cat and the canary
(1927) with live musical accompaniment by makia matsumura
: leonard nimoy thalia theater at symphony space (uws), $12 general, $9 seniors.
>>
10/26-31:
a dark castle entertainment horror film retrospective
:
gothika, orphan, house on haunted hill, thirteen ghosts
, and more. low cinema (ridgewood), $15.
>>
10/26 7pm:
night of the living dead
(1968) with a live score by morricone youth
: nitehawk (prospect park). $24.
>>
pets
10/24 12pm (rain date 10/25):
24th annual battery park city dog association halloween puppy parade
: wagner park, free admission.
>>
10/24 12pm:
fort greene pups’ 28th annual great pupkin dog costume contest
: fort greene park monument stairs. note: registration to compete is full. free to attend.
>>
10/24 12-3pm (rain date 10/25):
the annual riverside park pup halloween parade and costume contest
: starts at dinosaur playground on 96th st and ends at ellington’s cafe at 105th st. free admission.
>>
10/24 1-3pm:
fifth annual irving square park howl-o-ween costume contest
: irving square park (bushwick), $10 to register in the contest, free to attend.
>>
10/25 1-3:30pm:
the annual stuyvesant square park halloween dog parade and costume contest
: stuyvesant square park – east park dog run. free admission (donations welcome).
>>
10/25 1-4pm:
the annual domino park woof-o-ween + costume contest
: the fountain + seating steps (river st between s 3rd + s 2nd sts, williamsburg). free admission.

.

Brooklyn Navy Yard’s Annual Open House
Saturday, October 17
12-5pm
FREE
Check in at Building 77, 141 Flushing Ave
Discover the Brooklyn Navy Yard’s 300-acre innovative campus during their
Annual Open House
, part of Open House New York Weekend on October 17 from 12-5pm. Step inside the studios of businesses in fashion, design, and technology for exclusive behind-the-scenes access, along with wine tastings, food trucks, live art demos, and more.
This year, two unique tour tracks have been created to guide visitors on their journeys:
Creative Currents
– Creativity flows through the Brooklyn Navy Yard; home to hundreds of artists, ranging from painters to photographers to jewelers. They’ll be opening their studios to the public, inviting audiences in for a rare opportunity to view their work, learn about their processes, inspirations, and their journeys here at the Yard.
BNY Past, Present, and Future
– From our start in 1801 as a premiere ship building facility, the Navy Yard has always been on the cutting edge of manufacturing and technology. On BNY’s campus, rich history meets an innovative future, as we look ahead towards what’s next in the fields of space tech, green energy, robotics, and more. Come tour BNY’s waterfront campus and take in centuries of legacy, as well as the labs and studios where the tech of the future is being made.
No matter what route you choose, this day celebrates a dynamic campus of makers and offers artists, engineers, entrepreneurs, and neighbors alike the chance to connect, meet the businesses who call the Navy Yard home, and experience innovation up close.

astronomy on tap: ‘the dark night’ edition

>>

brooklyn books + booze

>>
tues 7-11pm:
sugar, we’re hoein down: halloween edition line dancing x emo night
: two worlds collide at this line-dancing party set to emo, alt, and pop-punk bangers (zero country). total beginner? they’ll teach you the steps. 3 dollar bill (bushwick), $15.
>>
tues 8pm:
contemporaneous ensemble / recap percussion / mantra percussion present: ‘seeing in the dark’
: join contemporaneous for their 2026-2027 season opener, ‘seeing in the dark,’ an evening of new music that offers different ways to light our path through the darkness. co-presented with mantra percussion and recap percussion. roulette intermedium (boerum hill), free admission.

the rocky horror picture show

the phantom of the opera

taste of science presents: ‘under pressure: decoding the weather machine’

what’s the worst that could happen? a comedy show: ouija board edition

the monster high mash: a monster high drag party

thursday

wnyc’s in conversation: the affordability series

nyc now
for a live podcast taping and community conversation with residents, business owners, and mta officials to discuss the long-promised expansion of the second avenue subway, along with the tension between new transit investment and displacement it has raised. light fare and trivia will follow. cccadi ilé oyin (east harlem), free admission.

colbert

fallon

>>

>>
🎃 thurs 7pm (weather permitting):
free outdoor movie
:
sinners
at mccarren park (williamsburg).
>>
thurs 7-11pm:
moma ps1 school nite

>>

goth sk8 halloween
: featuring gargoyle, llora, and nightwitch. xanadu (bushwick), $26.78 + $8 skate rental (or byo).
>>
thurs 8:30pm:
copacabana comedy
: catherine lindsay and dorian debose host a night of comedy inspired by the glamorous golden age of variety shows. tonight’s lineup includes grace johnson, keegan tindall, sammy anzer, noah snyder, and more. telephone room (bushwick), $8-10.
>>
thurs 8:30pm:
landline comedy at wild east brewing co.

(gowanus). tonight’s lineup includes mary houlihan (adult swim), mac o’hara (hulu), trent mabry (sirius xm), bridget mcguire, bria hiebert, and sam kochman. hosted by andre medrano. bonus: rsvp for a chance to win a free drink. free admission.

guillermo del homo:
pan’s labyrinth
20th anniversary drag tribute
: c’mon everybody (bed-stuy), $13.39.

miller theater’s pop-up concert series

scientific controversies: octopus umwelt

national geographic: secrets of the octopus
) and dr. caroline albertin investigate what the octopus can reveal about the nature of consciousness, perception, the origins of the mind, and what it means to be intelligent. hosted by barnard physics and astronomy professor and pioneer works director of sciences janna levin. food will be available for purchase, and stargazing with the amateur astronomers association will precede and follow the event. pioneer works (red hook), free admission (donations welcome).
>>

astronomy live: exploring cosmic building blocks
: join astrophysicist emily calamari at the american museum of natural history for a journey from the chemical building blocks found in meteorites to the swirling disks of gas and dust surrounding young stars, exploring how planets take shape and discovering what new observations are revealing about the origins of worlds throughout the universe. hayden planetarium space theater (uws), $20.

creative showcase vol. 7

the moth storyslam

Join Jill Weiner on Thursday 10/22 as she records her debut comedy special!
TWO SHOWS! 7pm & 9:30pm
at the Parkside Lounge (317 E Houston, Lower East Side)
Jill Weiner’s Debut Comedy Special (tentatively titled
SOUP FREAK
) is a darkly funny, silly, smart, and sharp hour of stand-up comedy. With topics ranging from Peloton to drug doing, dating a guy in a van to suicide by sea, Jill shares her deeply relatable perspective on the human condition while revealing her insecurities, memories, and, of course, her favorite soups, stews and stocks. From top to bottom (or, better yet, soup to nuts), Jill’s show maintains a high-energy level akin to a slumber party at 2am.
A fixture in the New York City comedy scene for over 11 years, Jill has performed at the city’s top clubs and independent shows. She also performs nationally, often featuring for Caitlin Peluffo and Michael Kosta.

Fan Therapy
), with special performances by Mark Benjamin (

national coffee day deals
: score a free drip coffee or cold brew at all
coffee project new york

krispy kreme
all day.
tues 6pm:
page break presents: stage break reading series with astra house
: four astra house books writers take the stage to read original short stories, one page at a time, alternating with audience members picked at random to join them (optional: enter your name to read). everyone gets a zine with the four stories, so you can follow along from your seat. presented by page break, a weekend reading retreat. mcnally jackson books at bklyn studios (downtown brooklyn), $10.
>>
tues 6:30pm:
pretty in pink
x
straight white men can’t dance
with jon cryer + addie tsai
: revisit the john hughes 80s classic
pretty in pink
(written by hughes and directed by howard deutch) on the big screen, followed by a q+a and book signing with author addie tsai and star jon cryer. journalist rich juzwiak moderates the discussion about the film and tsai’s new book,
straight white men can’t dance: american masculinity in film and popular culture
. ifc center (greenwich village), $18 general, $15 seniors. copies of the book will also be available for purchase.
>>
tues 7pm:
spider man total universe
with patrick a. reed + nick lowe
: pop culture historian patrick a. reed launches his fully-illustrated book tracing spider-man’s comic book history from
amazing fantasy #15
in 1962 to today, talking all things spidey with marvel’s spider-man editor nick lowe at your friendly neighborhood powerhouse arena (dumbo). powerhouse arena (dumbo), $5 admission includes a store gift certificate, $80 ticket option includes a copy of the book.
>>
tues 7pm:
this guy sucked
presents: draft of shame
: using sports drafting methods, podcast hosts/historians claire aubin (
this guy sucked
) and patrick wyman (
past lives
), along with commentator manny fidel (
no such thing
), assemble an elite team of america’s evil-est dead people and pit them against each other in a race to the bottom. caveat (les), $15 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $25+).
>>
tues 7pm:
punch puppet slam:
the princess bride
: a diverse group of puppet artists use a wide variety of puppet styles to tell the story of buttercup, westley, inigo, and the gang. the tank (midtown), $23.
>>
tues 8pm:
live band karaoke at arlene’s grocery
: pick your song, grab the mic, and be a star with your very own live band (nakatomi5) backing you up at arlene’s grocery (les). bonus: online ticket purchasers are entered in raffles to win prizes like drink tickets, skip-the-line song passes, or free admission to future shows. $10 adv, $15 day-of.
>>
sponsored

cookie

titanic

colbert
